title: Briefing for 2026-11-01
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-11-01: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts. European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%. Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates. The politics of President Lagarde's European Central Bank early exit — and who could replace her. Analysis: Kevin Warsh is keeping Wall Street guessing. It may be his most powerful tool. Here are five key takeaways from the Fed rate decision and Warsh news conference.
global: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city. India's opposition set to hold mega rally seeking election chief's resignation. How the downfall of Serbia's Vučiċ mirrored that of Hungary's Orbán. Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training. How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant. Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded.
philippines: [Time Trowel] Ube is taking over the world. So why are Filipinos still obsessed with rice?. They came home to the Cordillera and found more than they expected. Tovera-led La Salle wins 3rd straight as rival Ateneo falls in OT thriller. France braces for fresh unrest, government vows tough response.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
